jobs.title: Director, Revenue Strategy & Planning
jobs.location: Bay Area, CA, United States of America
jobs.description:
Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.

So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff. Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place. Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.

Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business, and we are helping sellers worldwide do the same.

The Role

We are seeking a Director, Revenue Strategy & Operations to take on the most important and least defined problems facing Block's revenue organization. This is a special projects role. You will be the person our leaders turn to when a question is significant, ambiguous, and needs a rigorous answer.

Your work will be defined by the strategic initiatives that matter most at the time, and it will change as our priorities change. Early on, that is likely to include areas such as sales forecasting, pipeline management, and capacity planning for our non-direct sales organizations. Over time, you may hand work off once it is running well, or take on something entirely new.

This is an individual contributor role. You will lead through analysis, judgment, and influence rather than headcount, partnering closely with Sales Strategy & Operations, Finance, Sales, Partnerships, Services, Data, and Systems. You will report to the Head of Revenue Strategy & Planning within the Revenue organization.

You Will

You will lead the strategic initiatives and special projects that surface across the revenue organization, taking each from an ambiguous question through analysis to a recommendation leaders can act on. The work will change as our priorities change. Some examples of projects you might work on include:

- Building our sales forecasting rhythm, including the methodology, data requirements, cadence, and standard of quality a credible forecast depends on, and driving its adoption across the business.

- Defining how we measure pipeline health and whether we have sufficient pipeline to support the sellers we have hired and the targets we have set.

- Capacity planning for our non-direct sales organizations, translating expected volume into the staffing, ratios, role mix, and hiring timing those teams require.

- Assessing whether an organization is structured and sized efficiently, and recommending how it should change as volume grows.

- Modeling the return we should expect from a partnership, investment, or new commercial motion.

- Shaping commercial deal economics, including what we offer, what we hold back, and the thresholds that should govern non-standard terms.

- Creating process, structure, and clear assumptions in areas where none exist today, and leaving behind something the organization can operate without you.

- Producing executive-ready recommendations that make assumptions, tradeoffs, risks, and required decisions clear in plain language.

You Have

- 10+ years of experience in Strategic Finance, Financial Planning & Analysis, Sales Strategy & Operations, Revenue Operations, management consulting, investment banking, or a related analytical field.

- A track record of owning ambiguous, high-visibility problems end to end, from framing the question through to a recommendation leaders act on.

- Range. You are equally comfortable building a recurring operating process and answering a one-time strategic question, and you can move between them without losing quality.

- Experience with sales forecasting, pipeline analysis, and capacity modeling.

- Strong financial and commercial judgment, and advanced modeling skills in Excel or Google Sheets and SQL. You can work with large, complex data sets and turn them into clear decisions.

- Strong executive communication and cross-functional influence. You can build alignment and drive outcomes without direct authority.

- A bias toward building. You create structure where it is missing rather than waiting for it, and you are comfortable being the first person to work a problem.

Bonus

- Experience in payments, financial technology, usage-based pricing, or another multi-product business with several routes to market.

- Distill complex findings into concise narratives and visualizations for executive-level decisions.

- Champion rigorous analytics, building dashboards, SQL queries, and automated reporting to surface insights at scale.

- 5+ years in investment banking, private equity, strategic or corporate finance, or management consulting (tech or financial-services focus is a plus)

- Experience building the financial analysis behind a commercial negotiation, contract, or partnership, including modeling deal structures and pricing mechanics, and translating signed terms into a forecast.

- Demonstrated intellectual curiosity: you probe beneath the surface and connect seemingly disparate data to form a strategic point of view.

- Ability to build a point of view from incomplete information: reading market and competitive signals, forming a recommendation, and defending it with senior stakeholders.

- Mastery of Excel / Google Sheets and comfort with SQL and modern AI-assisted analytics tools.

- Track record of owning work end to end, from an ambiguous starting question through to decision-making.

- Experience leading projects with multiple cross-functional partners in fast-paced environments.

- Passion for Block's broader purpose of Economic Empowerment and a commitment to building inclusive financial products.

Square is looking for an experienced operations excellence and business operations leader to build the operating system for global seller onboarding. Reporting to the Head of Global Onboarding Operations, this role will create the metrics, planning processes, reporting cadences, capacity models, and continuous improvement mechanisms that help the onboarding organization scale with discipline.

This role closely partners with Onboarding Operational leaders and is designed to create leverage across the full organization. The right candidate is highly analytical, structured, and action-oriented, with the ability to turn operational complexity into clear plans, dashboards, routines, and recommendations.

What You Will Own

Operating Cadence and Business Management

- Build and run the core operating cadence for global onboarding, including weekly, monthly, and quarterly business reviews.

- Create consistent reporting, decision forums, action tracking, and escalation mechanisms across regions and operating models.

- Partner with leaders to turn strategic priorities into measurable plans, milestones, and execution routines.

- Own the global onboarding KPI framework, including activation, time-to-value, NPS, cost-to-serve, SLA adherence, utilization, and quality.

Planning, Capacity, and Financial Support

- Lead capacity planning and workforce modeling across first-party, vendor, and BPO delivery motions in partnership with regional and partner operations leaders.

- Partner with Finance on budget inputs, forecasts, headcount planning, vendor spend analysis, cost-to-serve models, and ROI assessments.

- Support annual and quarterly planning by translating volume, productivity, service quality, and cost assumptions into operational plans.

Process Improvement and Standardization

- Identify friction in onboarding workflows, handoffs, tooling, data quality, and escalation processes.

- Drive process standardization, playbook development, documentation, and continuous improvement initiatives across regions.

- Partner with Product, Enablement, Analytics, and Operations teams to improve systems, automation, and operational effectiveness.

AI Leadership

- Drive the adoption of AI-enabled workflows across the onboarding organization by identifying high-impact use cases, standardizing best practices, and helping teams apply AI to improve quality, speed, consistency, and operational efficiency.

- Build playbooks, training materials, and operating routines that help onboarding teams use AI effectively for tasks such as knowledge management, call/document summarization, process adherence, quality review, performance insights, and frontline enablement.

- Measure the impact of AI-enabled improvements on onboarding outcomes, including time-to-value, cost-to-serve, team productivity, seller experience, quality, and consistency; use findings to scale what works across regions and delivery models.

What We Are Looking For

- 8+ years of relevant experience with a Master’s degree, 12+ years with a Bachelor’s degree, or equivalent experience in operations, business operations, strategy and operations, workforce planning, analytics, or operational excellence.

- Experience building operating cadences, dashboards, planning processes, KPI frameworks, and performance management routines.

- Strong analytical skills and comfort working with operational, financial, workforce, and performance data.

- Experience with capacity planning, forecasting, budget inputs, cost-to-serve analysis, or vendor spend analysis.

- Ability to manage complex cross-functional projects independently while aligning with senior leaders on objectives and decisions.

- Strong process improvement mindset, with experience standardizing workflows and driving measurable operational impact.

- Excellent communication skills, including the ability to turn ambiguous problems into clear plans, tradeoffs, and recommendations.

- Experience in fintech, commerce, SaaS implementation, customer operations, field operations, or scaled services delivery preferred.

- Experience improving workflows and customer outcomes using AI

Why This Role Matters

As the global onboarding organization scales, strong execution requires more than local management. This role creates the connective tissue across the organization: the metrics, planning discipline, insights, and routines that help leaders make better decisions and teams improve faster. By strengthening the operating system, this role improves seller outcomes, team accountability, and the scalability of Square’s onboarding model.

Initially built to take the pain out of peer-to-peer payments, Cash App has gone from a simple product with a single purpose to a dynamic ecosystem, developing unique financial products, including Afterpay/Clearpay, to provide a better way to send, spend, invest, borrow and save to our 50+ million monthly active customers. We want to redefine the world’s relationship with money to make it more relatable, instantly available, and universally accessible.

Today, Cash App has thousands of employees working globally across office and remote locations, with a culture geared toward innovation, collaboration and impact. We’ve been a distributed team since day one, and many of our roles can be done remotely from the countries where Cash App operates. No matter the location, we tailor our experience to ensure our employees are creative, productive, and happy.

The Role

You will join the Recon and Reporting team, which owns our post-transaction systems: the platform responsible for reconciling money, tracing the end-to-end flow of funds, and meeting our tax and regulatory reporting obligations to merchants, customers, and authorities worldwide. Reconciliation and financial reporting are essential to running a payments business, and given our transaction volume, this role has direct, measurable impact on financial accuracy and trust.

As a Senior Analyst on the team, you will independently own reconciliation and reporting workstreams end to end. You will be the subject matter expert who ensures the numbers tie out: reconciling card-network settlement and report files (Visa, Mastercard, and equivalents), along with data from acquirers, processors, and banks, against our internal payment and ledger data. You will translate ambiguous reconciliation and reporting needs into concrete metrics, controls, and automated solutions, drive discrepancies to root cause and resolution, and directly influence the team's roadmap and the priorities of our finance, accounting, and engineering partners. Our mantra: all funds in the right place, at the right time, for the right purpose.

You Will

- Independently prioritize, design, develop, and deploy end-to-end reconciliation and reporting solutions: matching logic, break dashboards, exception queues, settlement summaries, and standardized journals that feed downstream accounting, audit, and regulatory processes.

- Own time-sensitive daily, weekly, and monthly reconciliations across card networks, banking partners, processors, and internal transaction and ledger data, including full ownership of discrepancy management from detection through root cause, corrective action, and control improvement.

- Translate ambiguous business, finance, and regulatory needs into concrete measurement systems: define and roll out key metrics for the reconciliation and reporting domain (match rates, break aging, time-to-resolution, funding compliance, reporting SLAs) and ensure stakeholders interpret them in the correct context.

- Serve as the subject matter expert on settlement, funding, and money-movement flows; field questions on transaction lifecycles, data models, and the reconciliation tech stack from stakeholders and leadership.

- Own the design, development, and documentation of automated SQL-based reporting using best practices, navigating new and unfamiliar datasets to answer complex questions about the flow of funds.

- Work independently or partner with data engineering to design, build, validate, troubleshoot, and maintain the datasets and pipelines that power reconciliation and reporting, making sound trade-offs between accuracy, implementation effort, and complexity.

- Proactively identify control gaps, revenue leakage, manual toil, and upstream data-quality issues; drive the automation and process improvements that fix them, and monitor daily settlement and banking activity for irregularities.

- Own relationships with technical and non-technical stakeholders across Engineering, Product, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, and Compliance; directly influence the priorities, decisions, and roadmap of the team and its partners.

- Lead month-end close support for the domain: reconciliation reporting, standardized summaries, and audit-ready documentation, including supporting internal and external audits.

- Define business requirements and test plans for system changes, validate new processes and reconciliation capabilities before deployment, and partner with Engineering and Data teams to resolve bugs and ship enhancements.

- Help onboard and mentor other analysts, including reviewing code and evangelizing reconciliation and reporting best practices.

- Apply an AI-first mindset to improve the speed, quality, and insight of analytical work, and guide responsible AI use on the team.

You Have

- 5+ years of related experience in reconciliation, settlement, payment operations, accounting, or finance analytics with a Bachelor's degree (Finance, Accounting, Economics, a quantitative field, or similar); or 3+ years with a Master's degree; or equivalent work experience.

- Expert-level SQL, including owning the design, development, and documentation of automated SQL-based reporting, and the ability to navigate new datasets and answer complex questions independently.

- Demonstrated experience independently owning reconciliation, settlement, or financial reporting workstreams end to end, including defining metrics and driving them to adoption.

- Strong knowledge of accounting principles, double-entry concepts, and the mechanics of money movement, with the judgment to question the correctness and completeness of financial data.

- Experience partnering with data engineering (or working independently) to design, build, validate, and maintain data pipelines, with the ability to make sound technical trade-offs.

- Advanced Excel proficiency (complex formulas, pivot tables) and experience with reconciliation tooling and banking portals.

- Excellent communication skills: able to own senior stakeholder relationships, present findings and recommendations, and drive clear next steps in areas without clear ownership.

- Track record of proactively identifying and delivering process improvements and automation in a deadline-driven, high-accuracy environment.

Preferred Experience

- Deep experience with card-network reconciliation and settlement (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover), including network settlement, clearing, and report file formats.

- Strong familiarity with funds-transfer processes and rails (ACH, wire, SWIFT, RTP/FedNow) and the payments ecosystem: merchants, acquirers, issuers, processors, and program banks.

- Scripting skills (Python or similar) for data analysis and process automation.

- Experience with cloud data warehouses (e.g., Snowflake, BigQuery) and BI platforms (e.g., Looker, Tableau), including building governed reporting layers with SLAs.

- Exposure to interchange and fee/cost reconciliation, revenue-leakage detection, and tax or regulatory reporting regimes.

- Experience supporting audits, internal controls, or SOX-adjacent processes, and mentoring junior analysts.

- Curiosity about payments products and financial markets.

The Role

Cash App reaches 59 million monthly active customers, and top-of-funnel growth is accelerating. We're looking for a Growth Manager to be the GM for activation and habituation. You'll own the goals for how customers find their first meaningful moment in Cash App and turn it into a lasting habit, and you'll decide how to hit them.

This role blurs growth and product. You won't hand requirements off to someone else. On this team, you are the product owner for your growth levers. You'll set the strategy, own the roadmap and experiment backlog, and work directly with Engineering, ML, Design, and Analytics to ship.

Every lever is on the table: onboarding flows, in-app surfaces and prompts, eligibility logic, incentive mechanics, notifications, and customer communications across push, email, SMS, and in-app. You'll pick the lever most likely to move the metric, run the experiment, and scale what works.

You'll sit on the Cash App Engagement Marketing team, which gives you deep customer context, lifecycle craft, and a strong peer group. But this isn't a traditional marketing role. You'll be just as comfortable shipping a product change as you are writing and launching a message or building the model behind an upsell engine.

People who thrive here have come from growth product, growth marketing, lifecycle, business operations, and consumer analytics. What they share is a drive to own outcomes, an experimentation reflex, and the ability to move between strategy and the details.

What's Unique About This Role

- Scale. With 59M monthly actives and rapid top-of-funnel growth, your experiments read in days, not months, and your wins move numbers that matter.

- Real ownership. You own the goal and the levers. Your roadmap shapes what Cash App builds, not just what it sends.

- Every lever is fair game. Product changes, in-app experiences, incentives, and comms are all yours to test and combine.

- The AI frontier. You'll help define what growth looks like as decisioning becomes increasingly AI-driven. Every experiment you run feeds, and is shaped by, the AI and automation stack we're building.

You Will

- Own activation and habituation goals end-to-end as the GM for your area. Define the opportunity landscape, set strategy, decide where to invest, and deliver measurable impact on activation and retention.

- Own the roadmap and experiment backlog for your area. Score every idea against expected impact and effort, whether it's a product change, an in-app surface, an incentive, or a message.

- Run rapid experiments across a wide range of levers, including onboarding, post-onboarding upsell, contact opt-in, behavioral notifications, real-time intervention, mobile wallet adoption, referrals, churn prevention, and winback.

- Ship directly with Engineering, ML, and Design. That covers product changes like onboarding flows, in-app prompts, eligibility logic, and incentive mechanics, as well as the customer communications that support them.

- Diagnose your own funnel. Size opportunities, find friction, read experiment results, and iterate without waiting on an analyst.

- Push the frontier on AI decisioning and automation, and help define how growth work evolves as AI moves further into the decisioning layer.

- Bring what you learn back to the Engagement Marketing team so wins scale across Cash App's broader lifecycle programs.

- Influence strategy across Product, Analytics, Martech, Creative, and Brand as a true peer of these teams.

You Have

- 5+ years of experience in growth product, growth marketing, lifecycle marketing, CRM, growth strategy, business operations, or a consumer-facing analytical role in a B2C tech environment

- A track record of owning a growth goal end-to-end, from opportunity through measurable impact, including real ownership of what got built and shipped

- Experience shaping the product experience itself and working directly with engineers to ship it

- Comfort moving between strategy and hands-on execution. You're as willing to write and launch a message as you are to define a product change or build the model behind it.

- Strong data instincts. You can size an opportunity, build an impact model, and diagnose a funnel from first principles, and you're comfortable pulling and interpreting data yourself, whether through SQL, AI tools, or other means. Experience with data modeling or opportunity sizing frameworks required

- Deep experimentation experience. You know how to build a backlog, design rigorous tests, and use results to drive compounding improvements

- Hands-on experience with a CRM or marketing automation platform (e.g., Braze, Iterable, Salesforce Marketing Cloud), or strong reason to believe you'd ramp on one quickly

- Fluency with AI tools as a core part of how you work, with the ability to automate, accelerate, and scale output in ways that set a new standard for the team

- Clear, structured, takeaway-first communication. You can turn complex analysis and ambiguous situations into crisp strategy and actionable recommendations

Nice to Have

- Experience as a growth PM or in another role where you owned a product roadmap

- Experience with onboarding, activation, or referral programs specifically

- Familiarity with regulated or trust-sensitive products (e.g., fintech, financial services, or healthcare)

- Experience with incentive mechanics or in-app personalization

Technologies We Use and Teach

- Braze, Iterable, or similar CRM and marketing automation platforms

- SQL and AI-assisted analysis for self-serve opportunity sizing

- Design agentic AI workflows that pair LLM reasoning with deterministic, auditable decision layers for evidence analysis, control monitoring, classification, and assessment

- Build the evals, benchmarks, and calibration harnesses that keep automated governance honest

- Automate evidence collection and continuous control monitoring to replace point-in-time audit preparation

- Define the technical approach for ambiguous, cross-team problem spaces. This is an early-stage program, and you will frame problems as often as you solve them

- Partner with Security Governance Partners, Compliance, and Engineering teams to find the manual processes most worth turning into product

- Contribute to technical design discussions, evaluating the security and reliability properties of the platform itself

You Have

- 7+ years building production software in backend, platform, data, or security engineering

- Multi-year ownership of a production system, including on-call, SLOs, and the maintenance work that starts after launch

- Proficiency with at least one of Python, Kotlin, Java, or Go, and comfort reading unfamiliar codebases

- Experience with integration patterns: REST APIs, webhooks, authentication flows, event-driven architectures

- Experience pulling, normalizing, and joining data from multiple imperfect sources, and handling the edge cases gracefully

- Experience defining technical direction where the problem was ambiguous, and carrying it across team boundaries

- Attention to detail balanced with pragmatism about risk-based prioritization

Nice to have (optional):

- Working knowledge of a security or compliance framework such as PCI DSS, SOX, SOC 2, ISO 27001, or NIST. Prior GRC experience is not required; we can teach the governance side

- Languages & Frameworks: Python, Java, Kotlin, Go

- Infrastructure: AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD (Buildkite), event-driven architecture
